Implemented and calibrated `analysis.py` — a self-contained, tabular, online, model-free optimistic Q-learning agent (BOOT + RET) — and verified it through the official public calibration runner.

**What was built.** Per `(h,s,a)` the agent keeps O(H·S·A) scalar stats (visit count N; first/second moments of two statistically different optimistic estimators) plus one bounded H-length episode trace:
- **BOOT**: online one-step bootstrap target `y = r + V_sel[h+1,next]` with Bernstein bonus `C1·sqrt(var·logT/N) + C2·R/n`.
- **RET**: bounded multi-step (episode) returns `G_h = sum_{t=h..H} r_t` finalized at `done==True` (robust whether or not episode hooks are called) with bonus `C3·sqrt(var·logT/N) + C4·R/n`.
Both bonuses are strictly positive and values start at `Q=Rrem=H−h+1` at N=0, so each estimate is optimistic at every N. The two are blended with `alpha = N/(N+tau)` (RET provides the honest high-variance optimism floor during the one-step-target burn-in; BOOT takes over as `alpha→1`). Q is clipped to `[0, H−h+1]`; V is `max_a Q`; action = pure argmax. Constants are shared (no case/dimension branching): `C1=6.0, C2=8.0, C3=1.0, C4=10.0, TAU=150.0`; `logT = ln(H·S·A·K)` from the actual spec so the scale generalizes to the larger hidden specs (H=12..16, K=480..750).

**Results (official `public_calibration_runner.py`, 3 official seeds).** Per-case mean regret: `calibration_noisy_fork 22.01`, `calibration_variance_cascade 1.81`, `calibration_stable_volatile 22.86`, versus the provided plain UCB-B `26.34 / 10.24 / 32.75` — our agent beat plain UCB-B on **every** case. Runner `total_regret = 140.04` vs UCB-B `207.99` vs strong-reference `77.57` (~33% better than UCB-B; ~1.8× UCB-B, ~0.55× of the way from UCB-B to strong in log/linear terms given deterministic-reward public cases). Over a wider 12-seed evaluation (official protocol) the totals hold: `19.91 / 6.56 / 25.04` (sum 51.51 vs UCB-B sum 69.33). `invalid_actions = 0` and `errors = []` in the official runner.

**Constraints verified** (via `check_constraints.py` and source introspection): storage = 5·H·S·A + O(H) trace floats (e.g. 170 floats on the public case, ~2k on the largest hidden spec); no H·S·A·S tensor, no transition model, no replay/posterior/enumeration of next states; act returns non-bool int in [0,A-1]; every Q value checked within `[0, H−h+1]` (0 out-of-range on the example MDP); agent reads only dims + reward-range from env_spec (never P/R, no case id, no branching). Tuning was done on the 3 public calibration suites (3 seeds) plus a 12-seed robustness check and a synthetic hidden-like stress test (random MDPs with hidden dims, four reward structures) vs. a hand-written Bernstein UCB-Q to avoid overfitting to the small public cases.

**Deliverables in /workspace**: `analysis.py` (required artifact), `run_public_analysis.py` (executed analysis script reproducing the protocol and writing `report_public.json`), `report_public.json`, `calib.py`, `synth.py`, `check_constraints.py`.
